description: The >>PAGE [comment-text-1] compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.19) - page ejection plus documentation for the source listing. §2023:7.3.19.4 GR3 says a PAGE directive has no effect when no source listing is produced, so recognize-and-consume is the conforming disposition. The introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.16.3 GR3: 'If a source listing is not being produced, a PAGE directive shall have no effect'; and §2002:F.2 names it, its item 29: 'to specify page ejection'. 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.17: 'The PAGE directive specifies page ejection and provides documentation for the source listing') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.19.1).

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.19.2 general format: >> PAGE [ comment-text-1 ] — bracketed, so the operand is optional; §2023:7.3.19.3 SR2 states that comment-text-1 'is not checked syntactically', which is why this row's content check is the standard's own decision rather than a gap.

source:
>>PAGE PB725 PAGE DIRECTIVE
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725PG.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
